command: ETLANTIC_CP_TEST_URL=<isolated PostgreSQL service URL> uv run pytest -q tests/prefect -m prefect
result: The full live Prefect suite passed: 46 passed in 61.32s. This includes the separate dispatcher/close race, read-only dispatcher diagnostics, and the self-hosted Prefect/PostgreSQL Process-worker campaign.
assertions: Four bounded dispatcher ticks against an unavailable Prefect API left all three accepted submissions unclaimed, with no execution attempts or sink effects.

After Prefect API restart, one-item dispatch ticks drained the three-item backlog; separate Process-worker runs completed each target once, with one sink effect per accepted submission and nonnegative queue-age receipts.

Provider-free dispatcher diagnostics recorded four failed Prefect API preflights during the outage, then three successful remote create attempts; the queue-age high-water value was nonnegative and the snapshot contained no submission or flow-run identifiers.
A focused stale-correlation contract test recorded one missing remote run and one terminal remote failure without including either flow-run ID in diagnostics.

A Prefect Process flow-run process was held after the sink effect, successful report, and run.completed event were durable. While it was held, a separate dispatcher process claimed another accepted target and was held before remote creation.

Both independent processes were released to hard-exit. The worker flow run was observed as CRASHED or FAILED; the dispatcher exited at the pre-create fault point with a leased dispatch and no Prefect flow-run ID.

Worker recovery published the already committed result without creating a second sink effect. Dispatcher recovery reused the persisted creation key, linked a flow run, and completed the other target exactly once.

A deterministic close race held a PrefectDispatcher tick during remote verification. ManagedBackend.close requested drain and refused engine disposal while the tick was active; after the tick settled, a second close disposed the engine.

runtime.prefect_server: Separately supervised Prefect API backed by a dedicated PostgreSQL database
runtime.worker_backend_plugin: Test fixture loaded in a separate process from the test plugin path; this campaign did not claim an installed-wheel run.

limitations: The outage campaign repeats four bounded ticks and recovers a three-item backlog; it is not a long-duration or production-capacity backpressure qualification.
The simultaneous failure trace covers one dispatcher pre-create crash and one worker post-publication-event crash. Other concurrent fault combinations remain open.
This is local source-checkout evidence, not installed-wheel or remote CI evidence; production and independent third-party connector qualification remain open.
cleanup: The live worker campaign created uniquely scoped tenant, workspace, submission, deployment, table, and Prefect database identities.
The test drops the dedicated Prefect database and its sink/effect tables after completion; no phase-specific database remains.
